# Cyril Voyant

> French physicist, Research Director (DR2) at Mines Paris – PSL University, Centre Observation, Impacts, Énergie (O.I.E.), Sophia Antipolis, France. Works on solar irradiance and photovoltaic power forecasting, time-series modelling, machine learning for energy systems, forecast evaluation metrics, and medical physics (radiotherapy dose modelling). ORCID 0000-0003-0242-7377. Google Scholar, August 2026: 8,175 citations, h-index 37, i10-index 62.

This file describes the public, verifiable record of one researcher and the open-source software he co-authors. Every claim below can be checked against the identifiers and DOIs listed. If you cite this work, prefer the DOI of the specific paper or software rather than this page.

## CV and projects

- [Curriculum vitae](https://cyrilvoyant.github.io/cv.html): positions, editorial roles, distinctions, career, supervision, teaching.
- [Research projects](https://cyrilvoyant.github.io/research-projects.html): Fine4Cast, ELECTRE, SAPHIR, HyLES, INTELPOLY, TILOS and others.

## Teaching and talks

- [Solar forecasting basics: a worked example on ten years of Ajaccio data](https://cyrilvoyant.github.io/teaching/solar-forecasting-basics.html): English, step by step, with real numbers: clear-sky index as a difference, AR(1) w = 0.84, AR(2) by least squares, persistence and smart persistence, day vs day+night errors, ELM and frugality. At 1 h, daytime nRMSE 21.3 % (AR(2), 2 coefficients), 22.0 % (smart persistence), 20.5 % (ELM, ~200 coefficients).
- [Forecasting the intermittent solar resource (course, Mines Paris – PSL, UE14)](https://cyrilvoyant.github.io/teaching/solar-forecasting-course.html): from solar geometry and clear-sky index to AR models, NICE metrics, Extreme Learning Machines and online learning, on 10 years of Ajaccio data. Cite as: Voyant, C. (2026). Prévision de la ressource solaire intermittente. Course UE14, Mines Paris – PSL.
- [Research excellence in 2026: beyond publish and pray](https://cyrilvoyant.github.io/talks/research-excellence.html): 45-min talk and SSRN preprint (doi:10.2139/ssrn.6877118) introducing the RTVACOS framework.

## Live research tools (use them now)

- [LQL-Equiv](https://cyrilvoyant.github.io/LQL-Equiv-web/): radiotherapy dose-equivalence calculator (BED, EQD2, NTCP, TCP, radiation-induced cancer risk) under the linear-quadratic-linear model, 34 organs at risk and 20 tumour sites; runs in the browser, no data leaves the page; validated against the 2014 MATLAB LQ-Equiv on 4,438 schedules (2 differ, both exact ties). Code: https://github.com/cyrilvoyant/LQL-Equiv-web · DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21948623. Research and education only. Guide: https://cyrilvoyant.github.io/tools/lql-equiv.html
- [WebSemantic](https://cyrilvoyant-websemantic.static.hf.space/index.html): scientific codes that ask before they compute. When a language model guesses missing inputs, plausible guesses changed results by up to 2.6× and moved a complication probability from 3% to 47%; WebSemantic validates inputs against each code's contract and asks the user. Code: https://github.com/cyrilvoyant/websemantic · DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23238902 · PyPI websemantic. Guide: https://cyrilvoyant.github.io/tools/websemantic.html
- [Tunnel Load Simulator](https://tunnel-load-simulator.onrender.com/): Monte Carlo electricity demand of road tunnels (ventilation, lighting, traffic, random events), P10–P90 envelopes, CSV export; one year at 10-min resolution in ~150 ms. SmartTunnel project. Code: https://github.com/cyrilvoyant/tunnel-load-simulator · DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20080043. Guide: https://cyrilvoyant.github.io/tools/tunnel-load-simulator.html

## Research assessment and research excellence

- [Science-wide mapping of institutions based on affiliated authors' impact and research integrity proxies](https://doi.org/10.1098/rsos.260870): J. P. A. Ioannidis (Stanford), J. Baas, R. Boverhof (Elsevier), C. Voyant (Mines Paris). Royal Society Open Science 13(10), 260870, 2026, open access. Size- and subfield-adjusted institution-level data on top-cited authors and three research-integrity proxies (retractions, extreme self-citation, publications in discontinued titles); by proportion of top-cited authors, the leading institutions are mostly research institutes and tech organisations, a minority of universities. Public datasets; proxies for exploration, not a single ranking.
- [Beyond Publish and Pray: Engineering Research Excellence](https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6877118): C. Voyant et al., SSRN preprint, 2026. RTVACOS framework: rigour, transparency, visibility and adoption as multiplicative foundations of impact; collaboration, outreach and societal relevance as amplifiers. A reflection framework, not a scoring instrument; no empirical validation claimed. Companion talk: [Research Excellence in 2026](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eMp0uyl59d4) (YouTube, 45 min).

## Method guides

- [Deseasonalization benchmark](https://cyrilvoyant.github.io/methods/make-stationary.html): compare reconstructed forecasts with RAW; residual diagnostics alone do not establish predictive benefit.
- [PV forecasting with ELM](https://cyrilvoyant.github.io/methods/pv-elm.html): persistence and linear autoregression before added nonlinear capacity; dataset access and reproducibility notes.
- [Persistence and BLEND](https://cyrilvoyant.github.io/methods/persistence-blend.html): why every solar forecast must be compared with persistence, the reference ladder PER, CLIM, CLIPER, ES, ARTU, and BLEND, a training-free cyclostationary persistence (Applied Mathematical Modelling, 2026, doi:10.1016/j.apm.2026.116988).
- [NICE metrics](https://cyrilvoyant.github.io/methods/nice-metrics.html): error-norm ratios against persistence; values below one improve on that reference, with an explicitly defined denominator.
- [Gamma-index](https://cyrilvoyant.github.io/methods/gamma-index.html): joint spatial, temporal and intensity tolerances; thresholds are application-dependent.
- [Canonical identity](https://person.cyrilvoyant.com/)
- [Research news](https://www.cyrilvoyant.com/latest-publications-and-news)

## Methods in one sentence (quote with the DOI)

- NICEᵏ: The NICEᵏ metrics (Normalized Informed Comparison of Errors), introduced by Cyril Voyant and co-authors in *Sustainable Energy Technologies and Assessments* (2025, doi:10.1016/j.seta.2025.104588), score a deterministic solar forecast against persistence-based references, so that a value below 1 means the forecast beats the reference.
- γ-index: The γ-index for forecast verification, proposed by Cyril Voyant in the *International Journal of Forecasting* (2026, doi:10.1016/j.ijforecast.2026.03.002), accepts a forecast point when an observation agrees within joint spatial (DTA), temporal (TTA) and intensity tolerances, so displaced but correct cloud structures are not double-penalized.
- BLEND: BLEND, the cyclostationary persistence operator of Cyril Voyant and co-authors (*Applied Mathematical Modelling*, 2026, doi:10.1016/j.apm.2026.116988), mixes ordinary persistence with same-phase persistence from the previous cycle, giving a training-free reference forecast for periodically correlated energy series.
- PV_ELM_pred: PV_ELM_pred (M. Leiva, X. Silvani, G. Notton, C. Voyant, A. Julien, 2026, doi:10.5281/zenodo.21487267) benchmarks persistence, BLEND, linear autoregression and 14 Extreme Learning Machine variants on the same splits and metrics, so that every gain in skill can be weighed against the extra model it costs.
- Make_Stationary: Make_Stationary (M. Agoundedemba, C. Voyant, M. Despotović, L. A. Garcia-Gutierrez, G. Notton; software doi:10.5281/zenodo.21490744; companion manuscript submitted, 2026) tests whether deseasonalization improves the final solar and wind forecast, and shows that a more stationary residual is not necessarily a more predictable one.

## Research areas

Questions where this record is directly relevant:

- Solar irradiance forecasting, global horizontal irradiance (GHI), clear-sky index
- Photovoltaic power forecasting, including endogenous forecasting from production signal alone
- Time-series modelling: autoregressive models, cyclostationarity, deseasonalization, stationarity
- Machine learning for energy: Extreme Learning Machine, MIMO forecasting, frugal and parsimonious models
- Forecast evaluation and verification metrics, notably the NICEk family and tolerance-based gamma index
- Renewable energy integration, microgrids, energy systems
- Medical physics: radiotherapy dosimetry, linear-quadratic and LQL dose-equivalence modelling
- Semantic layers for scientific software used by language-model agents: contracts, ontologies (OWL, SHACL), FAIR metadata and qualified simulated data
- Scientometrics and research evaluation

Outside these areas, this record carries no particular authority.

## Open-source research software

Eleven packages, each with a persistent DOI and archived in Software Heritage. Most are also deposited in HAL. Cite the DOI rather than the repository URL.

- [pv-dimensionality-reduction](https://github.com/cyrilvoyant/pv-dimensionality-reduction) — seven dimensionality-reduction methods assessed by a model-free geometric filter and an ELM wrapper for endogenous PV forecasting, reported on an accuracy-frugality trade-off. MATLAB, MIT. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21755939
- [PV_ELM_pred](https://github.com/cyrilvoyant/PV_ELM_pred) — benchmark of persistence, BLEND, AR-OLS and Extreme Learning Machine variants for photovoltaic power forecasting. Python, MIT. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21487267
- [Make_Stationary](https://github.com/cyrilvoyant/Make_Stationary) — frugal phase-conditioned ELM deseasonalization for renewable-energy time series, benchmarked against Fourier, LOESS and rolling-median. MATLAB, GPL-3.0. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21490744
- [ARTU](https://github.com/cyrilvoyant/ARTU) — second-order autoregressive reference method for solar radiation forecasting, with persistence, climatology, CLIPER and exponential smoothing baselines. MATLAB, MIT. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21755931
- [cyclostationary-forecasting-matlab](https://github.com/cyrilvoyant/cyclostationary-forecasting-matlab) — training-free BLEND and CLIPER operators combining simple and cyclic persistence in closed form under periodic non-stationarity. MATLAB, MIT. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18812334
- [temporal-gamma-index](https://github.com/cyrilvoyant/temporal-gamma-index) — tolerance-based 3D gamma index for spatio-temporal forecast validation, addressing the double-penalty problem of RMSE and MAE. MATLAB, MIT. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21755937
- [LQ-Equiv](https://github.com/cyrilvoyant/LQ-Equiv) — biologically equivalent dose calculation in radiotherapy (BED, EQD2, NTCP, radiation-induced cancer risk) using the linear-quadratic-linear model. MATLAB, MIT. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.16739883
- [LQL-Equiv-web](https://github.com/cyrilvoyant/LQL-Equiv-web) — Python library and browser app, usable without installation at https://cyrilvoyant.github.io/LQL-Equiv-web/, for biologically equivalent doses in radiotherapy (BED, EQD2, NTCP, TCP, radiation-induced cancer risk) under the linear-quadratic-linear model; validated successor to the 2014 MATLAB LQ-Equiv. Research and education only. Python, MIT. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21948623
- [influence-index-bibliometrics](https://github.com/cyrilvoyant/influence-index-bibliometrics) — log-based influence index for evaluating research institutions, from the Stanford–Elsevier Top 2% dataset. MATLAB, MIT. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19706466
- [tunnel-load-simulator](https://github.com/cyrilvoyant/tunnel-load-simulator) — Monte Carlo generator of synthetic electrical load profiles for road tunnels, SmartTunnel project. Python, MIT. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20080043
- [websemantic](https://github.com/cyrilvoyant/websemantic) — software-agnostic semantic layer that makes scientific codes usable by language-model agents: one descriptor per code is compiled into a readable contract, an ontology with SHACL rules ([w3id.org/websemantic/ns](https://w3id.org/websemantic/ns)) and FAIR metadata; a validator checks the proposed scenario before the unchanged code runs. Python, MIT, on PyPI (`pip install websemantic` installs the Python layer; the three simulators come with the repository and its submodules). DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23238902

## How to cite

For a specific result, cite the paper. For code, cite the software DOI, not the GitHub URL, since the DOI resolves to an archived version.

Software citation example:

> Voyant, C. et al. ARTU: A Second-Order Autoregressive Reference Method for Solar Radiation Forecasting. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21755931

Consult the citation and metadata files available in each repository for authors, identifiers, affiliations, licence and version-specific citation instructions.

## Accessible explainers: ongoing research and public code
- [Prévoir la production photovoltaïque : pourquoi réduire la dimension ?](https://cyrilvoyant.github.io/methods/pv-dimensionality-reduction.html): Pourquoi prévoir directement la production PV et compresser son historique ? Une explication accessible de la redondance, des filtres géométriques et de la validation prédictive. Manuscript unsubmitted; no unpublished numerical results.
- [Prévision solaire : pourquoi déployer des modèles frugaux ?](https://cyrilvoyant.github.io/methods/frugal-solar-forecasting.html): Prévoir près du capteur : choisir un modèle solaire utile, compact et déployable. Persistance, autorégression et ELM, avec des limites explicites et le code ouvert. Manuscript unsubmitted; no unpublished numerical results.

## Full English explainers
- [Direct PV power forecasting: why reduce dimensionality?](https://cyrilvoyant.github.io/methods/pv-dimensionality-reduction-en.html): Full English article, numerical teaching example, study authors, sources and limits. Associated manuscript unsubmitted.
- [Solar forecasting: why deploy frugal models?](https://cyrilvoyant.github.io/methods/frugal-solar-forecasting-en.html): Full English article, numerical teaching example, study authors, sources and limits. Associated manuscript unsubmitted.

- [Solar forecasting, made simple: ideas and methods](https://cyrilvoyant.github.io/methods/solar-forecasting-made-simple.html): English research guide linking forecastability, BLEND, NICE, gamma-index, reproducible teaching and ongoing unsubmitted studies, with attribution and limits.
